text:
Maya K.: Heads up — saw a new p99 tail yesterday on prod pool-37 around 22:10 UTC while load hit ~18k concurrent. Suspect KV eviction thrash + kernel reselecting frequently.

Ashok P.: Yep, noticed it too. The trace looked like: lots of small microbatches, then a flurry of KV evictions, then kernel fallback for a few requests, then back to optimized kernel. Tail spikes ~600ms above baseline.

Liam H.: Do we have profiler snippet? rough numbers?

Maya K.: Pulled a short trace from the SLO tracer, redacted:
```
kv_evictions: 120/s
kernel_switches: 42 (dense<->quantized)
microbatch_size_p50: 6
microbatch_size_p95: 18
p95_latency: 85ms
p99_latency: 720ms (spike window)
cpu_wait_ms: +40ms during eviction events
```

Riley S.: Oof. kernel_switches 42 in 5m is nasty. That indicates we’re changing execution path mid-stream. Likely because KV hotset footprint crosses a threshold that triggers fallback kernels (memory layout/quant path).

Ashok P.: Correlated it with KV cache pressure metrics: working_set_size jumped ~12% as new keys came in, eviction rate crossed our soft-hysteresis, eviction bursts caused GC-like pauses while we reshuffled cache metadata. Combined with tiny microbatches increases scheduling jitter.

Maya K.: My quick theory: high concurrency + many small microbatches -> less effective prefix caching -> higher KV lookup misses for intermediate layers -> transient growth of active KV -> eviction -> kernel path change (e.g., enabling slower fallback to avoid OOM) -> tail spike. So the SLO hit is emergent from the interaction of microbatch sizing, cache eviction policy, and kernel selection thresholds.

Liam H.: That matches a flame I saw. Two possible mitigations: (A) warmset soft-reserve: keep a tiny reserved cache budget for hot keys to avoid immediate eviction; (B) hysteresis on kernel selection so we don't flip kernels until sustained signal. Both could be combined with temporary microbatch bump for hot connections.

Riley S.: Agreed. Quick pros/cons: warmset reserve reduces eviction churn but reduces effective cache capacity (cost). Kernel hysteresis reduces oscillation but risks running slightly suboptimal kernel for a short period. Microbatch bump reduces per-token overhead but increases p50 a bit.

Ashok P.: Proposed experiment: implement warmset soft-reserve = 8% of cache for top-N hot keys (LRU-weighted by recency+freq), kernel hysteresis window = 15s (require persistent signal), and adaptive microbatch: when eviction_rate > X, bump target_mb_size by +2 for affected workers for 30s. Canary on pool-37 with 5% traffic.

Maya K.: Nice. We should also add a new SLI: kernel_switch_count per minute and eviction_burst_count (evictions per second > threshold). Want alerting at kernel_switch_count > 10/min during steady state.

Riley S.: I'll add the metrics. Query sketches:
```
sum(rate(kernel_switches[1m])) by (pool)
sum(rate(kv_evictions[30s]) > 30) by (pool)  # burst count
```

Ashok P.: I can code the warmset guard in the cache manager. For canary: config keys
```yaml
warmset_reserve_pct: 8
kernel_hysteresis_seconds: 15
adaptive_mb_delta: 2
adaptive_mb_window_seconds: 30
```
I'll put it behind remote flag `evict-warmset-v1`.

Maya K.: Timeline? If Ashok can ship a patch + tests in 2 days, we can canary 24h and evaluate p95/p99. Also include the profiler probe to capture kernel_switches and eviction context.

Ashok P.: Sounds good. I'll open PR today, add unit tests and a deterministic sim to validate no regressions under low load.

Liam H.: For evaluation, capture these buckets: p50/p95/p99, kernel_switch_count, eviction_rate, cpu_wait_ms, and throughput. Baseline window = last 6h before canary. We'll run canary 24h and compare delta.

Riley S.: I'll wire dashboards + a dashboard diff panel and set an automated job to snapshot pre/post. Also add a perf regression bot check for p99 > baseline + 10%.

infra-bot: deploy started for evict-warmset-v1 canary on pool-37 (5% traffic). CI passed.

Maya K.: Great — once canary is live, let's watch for kernel_switch_count and eviction_burst_count. If either drops ~50% and p99 improves, we promote. If p50 regresses > 3% we roll back.

Ashok P.: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8423 (draft). I'll post test sim results in the thread once CI completes.

Liam H.: One more safety idea: if kernel_hysteresis holds kernel in slower mode for more than 2x expected, auto-revert that worker to previous kernel to avoid prolonged regressions. Might be overcomplicated for v1.

Maya K.: Capture that as v2. For now let's run v1, collect metrics. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

Riley S.: Added dashboard and alert. Will ping in thread when graphs populate.

Ashok P.: CI is green, sim shows eviction bursts down 48% in the synthetic hot-key churn scenario and kernel_switches down 60%. Posting sim log excerpt: 
```
[SIM] hot_key_churn=heavy -> evictions/s: 92 -> 48
[SIM] kernel_switches/5m: 98 -> 39
[SIM] p99_latency_ms: 820 -> 420
```

Maya K.: Excellent. We'll be cautious in prod but optimistic. Follow-ups: Ashok -> 📌 finish canary rollout and post 6h snapshot. Riley -> 📌 verify alerts. Liam -> 📌 prepare rollback playbook. I'll review PR today.

Ashok P.: On it.
